messages.author: 7c8a33455cb7050c
messages.subject: odd variogram signals
parts:
Hi, I've run into some odd variograms in my caribou data - for lack of a better description, some of them are coming out "squiggly".  Besides showing there is little evidence for range residency, Im not sure how to interpret these.  What would cause this signal?  

The satellite collars I'm analyzing have a programmed geofence - within a certain area, sampling is hourly, outside the area sampling is 3 times a day.  Would switching between the sampling regimes cause this "squiggly" signal?  

Thanks for taking a look!  R

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] odd variogram signals
parts:
Hi Robin,

This is pretty common, and as you guessed, is caused by the differing sampling intervals. You can account for it in the variogram using dt=c(1,8) %#% “hour” in the variogram function.

Jesse

Sent via mobile--I apologize for excess brevity

messages.subject: Re: odd variogram signals
parts:
Hi Robin,

There is some information in vignette('variogram') https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/variogram.html#irregular-sampling-schedules
and also in an appendix of the cited reference:

C. H. Fleming, J. M. Calabrese, T. Mueller, K.A. Olson, P. Leimgruber, W. F. Fagan, “From fine-scale foraging to home ranges: A semi-variance approach to identifying movement modes across spatiotemporal scales”, The American Naturalist, 183:5, E154-E167 (2014) doi:10.1086/675504.

If there is any other information needed, then please let me know.

Best,
Chris
